It seems that whoever read it in this way meant by major sin: polytheism, as Al-Farra’ used to say: It seems that I recommend for whoever reads major sins to lower the indecencies, so that the major sins are added to a group if they are a group. He said: I did not hear any of the reciters lower the indecencies. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two readings, each of which has been recited by scholars among the reciters, with their meanings being close, so whichever of them the reciter recites is correct. And His statement:
h
When they become angry
, they forgive. God Almighty says: And
h
when they become angry
with someone who has committed a crime against them, they forgive the one who committed his sin, and they pardon him for the punishment of his sin.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of the statement: Major sins.
The majority of the reciters of Medina read it unanimously in this way in An-Najm.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as major sin with the singular in both of them.

It seems that whoever read it in this way meant by major sin: polytheism, as Al-Farra’ used to say: It seems that I recommend for whoever reads major sins to lower the indecencies, so that the major sins are added to a group if they are a group.
He said: I did not hear any of the reciters lower the indecencies.

The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two readings, each of which has been recited by scholars among the reciters, with their meanings being close, so whichever of them the reciter recites is correct.

x: And His statement:
h
And those who responded to their Lord and established prayer God Almighty says
h
And those who responded to their Lord

when He called them to His Oneness, and to acknowledge His Oneness and to disavow the worship of everything worshipped besides Him, and established prayer the obligatory prayer within its limits and at its appointed times, and their affair is [determined by] consultation among themselves He says: And if a matter divides them, they consult among themselves, and from what We have provided them they spend He says: And from the wealth We have provided them they spend in the way of God, and they fulfill the rights imposed upon them for its people of zakat and spending on those whose expenses they are obligated to spend. Ibn Zayd used to say: What is meant by His statement
h
And those who responded to their Lord
... the verse is the Ansar.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said and he recited: And those who avoid major sins and immoralities, and when they are angry, they forgive. He said: So he began with them,
h
And those who responded to their Lord

the Ansar and established prayer and there was no Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them, and their affair is by consultation among them and there was no Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them either.

x: God Almighty says: And those who, when they are wronged and assaulted, they defend themselves. Then the people of interpretation differed about the aggressor whom God Almighty praised as the victor after his aggressing against him.
Some of them said: He is the polytheist if he aggressed against the Muslim.
Who said that: Yunus told me, he said:

c: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: He mentioned the emigrants as two types, a type that forgave, and a type that retaliated, and he recited: And those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, and when they are angry, they forgive. He said: So he began with them: And those who responded to their Lord… until His saying: And from what We have provided them, they spend. They are the Ansar. Then he mentioned the third type and said: And those who, when they are wronged, defend themselves. From the polytheists.

x: Others said: Rather, it is every wrongdoer, so he praised the one who defended himself from him.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And those who, when injustice befalls them, take revenge

, he said: They take revenge on those who have wronged them without having transgressed. This second statement is more correct in that, because God did not specify one meaning over another, but rather praised everyone who rightfully takes revenge on those who have wronged them.

x: What is there in taking revenge of praise?
Indeed, in establishing the oppressor on the path of truth and punishing him with what he deserves is a correction of him, and in that is the greatest praise.

And His statement, And the recompense for an evil deed is an evil like it. We have previously explained the meaning of that, and that it means: The recompense for the evil deed of the wrongdoer is his punishment with what God has made obligatory upon him. Even though it is a punishment from God that He has made obligatory upon him, it is still an offense to him. And evil is the evil deed, and that is similar to the statement of God, the Exalted, the Majestic, And whoever brings evil will not be recompensed except with the like thereof.
r
(Al-Anʿam: 160)
It has been said that the meaning of that is that the speaker makes the evil word obligatory with the like thereof.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Yaqub told us that Abu Bishr told me:
m: I heard Ibn Abi Nujayh say regarding His statement:
h
And the recompense for an evil act is an evil act like it
, he said: He says, May God disgrace him, and he says, May God disgrace him.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it
, he said: If someone insults you with an insult, insult him back with the same, without transgressing. Ibn Zayd used to say something about that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding And those who, when they are wronged, take revenge from the polytheists, “
h
And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it

. But whoever pardons and makes amends”… the verse, he did not command you to pardon them because he loved them. And whoever retaliates after having been wronged - against those there is no blame, then all of this was abrogated and he commanded him to wage jihad. So according to what Ibn Zayd said, the interpretation of the statement is: And the recompense for an evil from the polytheists to you is an evil like it from you to them, if you pardon and make amends in the pardon, then your reward for your pardoning them is with God, for He does not like the disbelievers. This is based on his statement, like the statement of God, the Exalted, “But whoever has transgressed against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you. And fear God” Al-Baqarah 2:194. The one who said this has a point. However, what is correct in our view is that the verse should be taken literally unless it is transferred to the inner meaning, which must be accepted. And a ruling in a verse should not be ruled to have been abrogated except by a report that eliminates the excuse, or by an argument that must be accepted. His argument in his statement,
h
And the recompense for an evil act is an evil act like it

, has not been proven, that it refers to the polytheists and not the Muslims, nor that this verse was abrogated, so we accept it as such. And His statement: But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is due from God. God, the Most High, says: Whoever pardons someone who has wronged him, and forgives him for it, and does not punish him for it, while he is able to punish him, seeking the pleasure of God, then his reward for pardoning him is due from God, and God will reward him according to His reward. Indeed, He does not like the wrongdoers. God, the Most High, says: God does not like the people of injustice who transgress against people and wrong them in ways other than what God has given them permission to do.

x: God the Most High says: And whoever retaliates against those who wronged him after he was wronged, “against those there is no blame. He says: Those who retaliate against them have no blame or harm against them, because they retaliated against them justly. And whoever takes his right from someone who is entitled to it, and does not transgress, is not wronged and will not be blamed.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of this.
Some of them said: It refers to everyone who retaliates against someone who wronged him, whether the wrongdoer is a Muslim or a disbeliever.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzayʿ told me, he said: Muʿadh told us, he said: Ibn ʿAun told us, he said:
m: I was asking about the verse And for him who vindicates himself after being wronged…, then ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn Judʿan told me, on the authority of Umm Muhammad, his father’s wife. Ibn ʿAun said: They claimed that she used to enter upon the Mother of the Believers. She said: The Mother of the Believers said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered, and Zaynab bint Jahsh was with us. He started doing something with his hands, but did not notice her. I moved his hand until I made him notice her, so he stopped. Zaynab came and pushed Aisha away, but he forbade her, by my father, to stop. He said to Aisha: ‘Captivate her.’ So she cursed her and overpowered her. Zaynab went and came to ʿAli and said: ‘Aisha is attacking you and doing things to you.’ Then Fatimah came, and he said to her: ‘By the Lord of the Kaʿba, she is the love of your father.’ She turned away and said to ʿAli: ‘I said such and such to him.’ He said: ‘And ʿAli came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.’” So talk to him about it.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And for he who retaliates after being wronged... the verse, he said: This is about scratching that occurs between people.

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
But whoever retaliates after being wronged - against them there is no blame
, he said: This is regarding what happens between people in terms of retaliation. If a man wrongs you, it is not permissible for you to wrong him.

x: Others said: Rather, it means retaliating against the polytheists, and he said: This is abrogated.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement:
h
But whoever retaliates after being wronged - against them there is no blame

, he said: For whoever retaliates after being wronged among the believers, he has retaliated against the polytheists. This has been abrogated, and this is not in the case of the people of Islam, but in the case of the people of Islam about whom God Almighty said: Repel evil with that which is better, then he between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend.
r
(Fussilat 41:34)
The correct statement is to say that it refers to everyone who retaliates against his oppressor, and the verse is decisive and not abrogated for the reason that was explained in the verse before it.

x: And His statement:
h
The path is only against those who wrong people

. God Almighty says: The path for you, O people, is only against those who transgress against people unjustly and aggressively, by punishing them for their injustice, not against those who take revenge on those who wronged them and take their right from them. And His statement:
h
And they transgress upon the earth without right

means: And they transgress upon the earth the limit that their Lord has permitted them to do, to what He has not permitted them to do, and they spread corruption therein without right. Those will have a painful punishment means: So those who oppress people and transgress upon the earth without right will have a painful punishment from God on the Day of Resurrection in Hell.

And God Almighty says: But whoever is patient in the face of the wrong done to him, and forgives the wrongdoer for his crime against him, and does not take revenge on him while he is able to take revenge, seeking the pleasure of God and His great reward - Indeed, that is of the matters [worthy of] determination. He says: His patience in that and His forgiveness of the sin of the wrongdoer is of the matters worthy of determination that He has urged His servants to do, and He has determined for them to act upon.

And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no protector after Him. He says: And he whom God lets down from guidance, there is no protector to follow him, guide him to the right path, and direct him after God has led him astray. And you will see the wrongdoers when they see the punishment. God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: "And you will see the disbelievers in God, O Muhammad, on the Day of Resurrection when they witness the punishment of God, saying to their Lord: "Is there any way back for us, O Lord?" ... This is like His saying: "
h
And if you could but see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord

, [saying], 'Our Lord, we have seen and we have heard.'" (al-Sajdah 32:12) ... the verse, the poor seek forgiveness at a time other than the time for seeking forgiveness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement, Is there a way back? He means to the world. The Arabists differed about the reason for the introduction of <in>in His statement: Indeed, that is of the matters of determination with the introduction of the lam in His statement:
h
And for whoever is patient and forgives
. The grammarian of Basra used to say about that: As for the lam in His statement:
h
And for whoever is patient and forgives

, it is the lam of initiation. As for that is that, its meaning, and God knows best, is that that is of it of the determination of matters. He said: You might say: I passed by the house the cubit of a dirham, meaning a cubit of it is worth a dirham, and I passed by a barley qafiz of it is worth a dirham. He said: As for the introduction of <in>in this place, it is like “Say: Verily, the death from which you flee—it will surely meet you” (al-Jumu’ah 48:8). It is permissible to begin a statement, and this is if the statement is long in this place.

x: Some of them found this statement wrong and said: When the Arabs insert the lam at the beginning of the conditional sentence, they respond with the responses of faith with ma, la, and if and the lam. He said: This is from that, as He said: If they are expelled, they will not go out with them (al-Hashr 59:12) and And if they are fought, they will not aid them; and if they aid them, they will turn their backs and then will not be aided (al-Hashr 59:12). So la and lam came as an answer to the first lam. He said: If he had said: If I stand, I will surely stand, it would have been permissible and there would be no need for a pronoun, because the answer to an oath may or may not have a pronoun. Don’t you see that you say: If I stand, I will surely stand and not stand, and I will surely stand, and you do not bring a pronoun. He said: As for their saying: I passed by Dar al-Dhira’ for a dirham and by a qafiz’s wheat for a dirham, the pronoun must be connected to the first, and the pronoun is only omitted in it because the second is a division of the first: I passed by wheat, some of it for a dirham and some of it for a dirham.

So since the meaning is a division, the pronoun was omitted. He said: As for starting with in in every place if the speech is long, it is not permissible to start with anything except the meaning: Say, Indeed, the death that you are escaping from, then it is a response to a recompense, and it is as if he said: What you fled from of death, it will meet you. This second statement is more correct in my opinion for the reasons we mentioned.
God Almighty says: And you will see, O Muhammad, the wrongdoers turning away from the Fire,
h
humbled by humiliation
. He says: submissive and humbled.

c: Yunus told us, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said:
m: Khushu’ is fear and awe of God Almighty. And he recited the words of God Almighty, When they saw the punishment… to His saying,
h
Humbled by humiliation
. He said: The fear that descended upon them humiliated them and they were humbled by it.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement, humbled, he said: submissive due to humiliation. And His statement, looking from a hidden corner, he said: These wrongdoers will look at the Fire when they are presented to it from a hidden corner.

x: The people of interpretation differed over the meaning of His statement, from a hidden corner.
Some of them said: It means: from a humiliated corner. It is as if the meaning of the statement is: from a hidden corner due to humiliation.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: And you will see them presented to it, humiliated by humiliation... to his statement: from a hidden side meaning by hidden: humiliated.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty, from a hidden glance, he said, humiliated.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that they steal glances.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, They look from a hidden corner, he said: They steal glances.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us,
m: Asbat said, on the authority of Al-Suddi, From a hidden corner, he said: They steal glances. The Arab scholars differed on this.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He made the eye the eye, as if he said: And their sight is from a weak eye, and God knows best. He said: And Yunus said: From the end is like the end, just as the Arabs say: I hit him with the sword, and I hit him with the sword. Another of them said: It was said from the hidden side because he does not open his eyes, but rather sees with some of them.

Others among them said: It was said from a hidden side because they look at the fire with their hearts, because they will be gathered blind. The correct statement about this is the statement we mentioned from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, which is that its meaning is: They look at the Fire from a humiliated perspective, and God’s description, may He be glorified and exalted, is to conceal the humiliation that has overwhelmed them, until their eyes almost sunk and disappeared.
And His statement,
h
And those who believed said
, ‘Indeed, the losers are
h
those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection
,’ God, the Exalted, says: And those who believed in God and His Messenger said, Indeed, the deceived are
h
those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection
in Paradise, as Muhammad told us, he said:

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection

, he said: They will lose themselves and their families in Paradise. And His statement: Indeed, the wrongdoers will be in a lasting punishment. God Almighty says: Indeed, the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection will be in a lasting punishment from God, fixed upon them, that will not be removed from them, will not be destroyed, and will not be lightened.

x: God Almighty says: And when God punishes these disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, there will be no protectors to protect them from God’s punishment, nor to take revenge for them from their Lord for the punishment He has inflicted upon them, other than God. And he whom God sends astray, for him there is no way. He says: And he whom He lets down from the path of truth, for him there is no way to reach it, because guidance and misguidance are in His hand, not anyone else’s.
And His statement:
h
Respond to your Lord

, God Almighty says to those who disbelieve in Him: Respond, O people, to the caller of God, and believe in him and follow him in what he has brought to you from your Lord, before there comes a Day from God of which there is no repelling. He says: Nothing can repel its coming when God brings it, and that is the Day of Resurrection. You will have no refuge that Day. God Almighty says: You will have no fortress, O people, in which to take refuge, or to which to seek protection from the punishment of God that will descend upon you because of your disbelief in Him, which was in this world. And you will have no denial. He says: Nor will you be able to change what will befall you on that Day, nor will you be able to take revenge from Him if He punishes you with what He punishes you with. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Those who said that: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said:

c: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
You have no refuge
he said: from a protector. And his statement: from Nakir he said: a supporter who will support you.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: You will have no refuge that Day to which you will resort, and you will have no denier meaning: from glory you will be proud.

x: God the Most High says: If these polytheists, O Muhammad, turn away from the truth you have brought them and the guidance you have called them to, and they do not respond to you and refuse to accept it from you, then leave them, for We will not send you to them as a watcher over them, to record and count their deeds. Upon you is only the conveyance means: You are only required, O Muhammad, to convey to them the message with which We sent you. If you convey that to them, then you have fulfilled your duty. And indeed, when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it means: If We enrich the son of Adam and give him plenty from Us, and that is the mercy that He, the Most High, mentioned, he rejoices in it: He says: He rejoices in what We have given him of wealth and what We have provided him of wealth and abundance of money. And if misfortune befalls them means: If poverty, hardship, and hardship befall them, because of what their hands have put forth means: Because of what they have put forth of disobedience to God as punishment for his disobedience to Him, his denial of God’s blessing.

And despair of the report, Indeed, man is ungrateful. God Almighty says: Indeed, man is ungrateful for the blessings of his Lord, he enumerates the calamities, and denies the blessings. Rather, He said, And if a misfortune befalls them, so He brought out the ha’ and the mim as a metaphor for the plural of males. And man was mentioned before that in the sense of one, because it is in the sense of the plural.

God Almighty says: To God belongs the dominion of the seven heavens and the earths. He does with His dominion what He wills, and creates what He loves for His creation. He grants to whomever He wills of His creation female children without males, by making every pregnancy his wife bears from him female. And He grants to whomever He wills males means: He grants to whomever He wills males among them, by making every pregnancy his wife bears male, with no female among them.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Or He pairs them up, males and females. He said: He mixes them. He says: Marriage: that a woman gives birth to a boy, then gives birth to a girl, then gives birth to a boy, then gives birth to a girl.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He gives to whom He wills females and He gives to whom He wills males
, God, our Lord, is able to do that, to give to a man males without a female, and to give to a man males and females, and bring them all together for him.
h
And He makes whom He wills barren
, meaning he will not have children.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty,
h
He gives to whom He wills females and He gives to whom He wills males
, there are no females with them, or He pairs them with males and females, he said: He gives them females and males,
h
and He makes whom He wills barren
so that he does not have children.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And He renders barren whom He wills
, meaning: He does not impregnate.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And He makes whom He wills barren
, he does not give birth to one or two.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd God told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
He gives to whom He wills females and He gives to whom He wills males
, “There is no female among them,” Or He pairs them with males and females, “A woman gives birth to a male once and a female once,”
h
And He makes whom He wills barren
, “He does not give birth to children.” Ibn Zayd said about the meaning of his saying: Or He marries them what:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Or He pairs them as males and females
, he said: Or He makes one male and one female twin. This is His statement:
h
Or He pairs them as males and females

. And His saying: He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful means that God Almighty says: God has knowledge of what He creates and the ability to create whatever He wills. Nothing of His creation is beyond His knowledge, and nothing He wants to create is beyond His power.

x: God Almighty says: It is not for a human being from among the children of Adam that his Lord should speak to him except by revelation which God reveals to him as He wills, or by inspiration, or by something else. Or from behind a veil means: or He speaks to him in such a way that he hears His words but does not see them, as He spoke to His Prophet Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace. Or He sends a messenger means: or God sends from among His angels a messenger, either Gabriel or someone else. And He reveals, by His permission, whatever He wills.
that messenger reveals to the one to whom he is sent, by the permission of his Lord, whatever He wills.
Meaning: whatever his Lord wills to reveal to him of commands and prohibitions, and other messages and revelations. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: in the words of God Almighty, And it is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation, He reveals to him, or from behind a veil, God spoke to Moses from behind a veil,
h
or He sends a messenger to reveal
by His permission what He wills, he said Gabriel brings the revelation. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement:
h
Or He sends a messenger to reveal

, so the majority of reciters of the regions read it as yuyuhi with the accusative of the ya’ in apposition to yusurulu, and they placed yusurulu in apposition to the place of revelation and its meaning, because its meaning is: It is not for a human being that God should speak to him except that He reveals to him or sends to him a messenger who reveals, by His permission, whatever He wills. Nafi’ al-Madani read it as yuyuhi with the sending of the ya’ in the nominative case in apposition to yusurulu, and with the nominative of yusurulu as the subject. And His statement:
h
He is Most High

, Most Wise means that God Almighty says: He - meaning Himself, may His praise be glorified - is above all things, elevated above them, and has power. Wise: meaning: He is wise in His management of His creation.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement: Or He sends a messenger to reveal, so the majority of reciters of the regions read it as yuyuhi with the accusative of the ya’ in apposition to yusurulu, and they placed yusurulu in apposition to the place of revelation and its meaning, because its meaning is: It is not for a human being that God should speak to him except that He reveals to him or sends to him a messenger who reveals, by His permission, whatever He wills.
Nafi’ al-Madani read it as yuyuhi with the sending of the ya’ in the nominative case in apposition to yusurulu, and with the nominative of yusurulu as the subject.

x: He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command
, and just as We revealed to all of Our messengers, thus We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, this Qur’an, a spirit of Our command: He says: a revelation and mercy of Our command.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of the spirit in this context.
Some of them said: It means mercy.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: A spirit from Our command, he said: A mercy from Our command.

x: Others said: It means: a revelation from our command.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command

, he said: A revelation of Our command. We have previously explained the meaning of the soul by mentioning the differences among the people of interpretation regarding it, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And His statement:
h
You did not know what the Book

was, nor what faith was, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: You did not know, O Muhammad, what the Book and faith were that We gave you. But We made it a light, meaning: But We made this Qur’an, which is the Book, a light, meaning a light for the people, so that they may be illuminated by its light that God made clear in it, and it is His explanation that He made clear in it, from what they have in it in acting upon it is guidance, and salvation from the Fire. We guide with it whom We will of Our servants, meaning: We guide with this Qur’an, so the ha in His statement with it is from the mention of the Book. What he means by his saying:
h
We guide with it whomever We will

is: We direct to the right path, which is faith in God. Whosoever We will of Our servants means: We guide with it whomsoever We will of Our servants to the straight path. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: h
You did not know what the Book

was, nor what faith was, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. But We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants, meaning the Qur’an. And the Most High said, But We have made it, and He made the ha’ singular, and it was mentioned before the Book and faith, because what was meant by it was to describe the Book.

x: Some of them said: He meant faith and the Book, but he made the ha’ singular, because the nouns of actions all have the verb in the plural, as one says, I like your coming and going, so they make them singular. And His saying: And indeed, you guide to a straight path. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And indeed, O Muhammad, you guide to a straight path, our servants, by calling to God and explaining to them.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And indeed, you guide to a straight path, God Almighty said: And for every people there is a guide (al-Ra’d 13:7) a caller who calls them to God Almighty.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And indeed, you guide to a straight path. He said: Every people has a guide.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And indeed, you guide to a straight path. He said: You call to a straight religion.

x: The path of God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. God, the Most High, says: "And indeed, you are guiding to a straight path, which is Islam, the path of God to which He has called His servants, to whom belongs the dominion of all that is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He has no partner in that." The second path is a translation of the first path. And His, the Most High, saying: To God do all matters return. He, the Most High, says: To God, O people, do your matters return in the Hereafter, and He will judge between you with justice.
Are not their affairs in this world up to Him?
Even though all of that is managed by Him, they have rulers and governors who look after their affairs, and on the Day of Resurrection they will have no ruler or authority other than Him.
Therefore it was said: All affairs there will return to Him, even though all of them are up to Him and in His hand is their judgment and management in every situation.
Commentary on Sūrat Consultation (al-Shūrā). In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
